ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$. Point D is on the extension line of AB, and CD is connected. If $AB = 2BD$ and $\tan\angle BCD = \frac{2}{3}$, what is the value of $\frac{AC}{BC}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $DM\perp BC$ from point D, intersecting the extension of BC at point M,\\
$\because$ $\angle ACB=\angle DMB=90^\circ$, $\angle ABC=\angle DBM$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABC\sim \triangle DBM$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{BD}{AB}=\frac{BM}{BC}=\frac{DM}{AC}$,\\
$\because$ AB＝2BD,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{BD}{AB}=\frac{BM}{BC}=\frac{DM}{AC}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
In $\triangle CDM$,\\
since $\tan\angle MCD=\frac{2}{3}=\frac{DM}{CM}$, let DM＝2k, then CM＝3k,\\
also $\because$ $\frac{BM}{BC}=\frac{1}{2}=\frac{DM}{AC}$,\\
$\therefore$ BC＝2k, AC＝4k,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AC}{BC}=\frac{4k}{2k}=\boxed{2}$.

The figure indicates that in triangle ABC, ∠ACB is a right angle. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, draw an auxiliary line: from D draw a perpendicular to the line on which BC lies, with foot of the perpendicular M, and M is on the extension of BC. Because AC ⟂ BC and DM ⟂ BC, ∠ACB = ∠DMB = 90°. Also because A, B, and D are collinear, and C, B, and M are collinear, ∠ABC = ∠DBM. Therefore △ABC ∼ △DBM. From the proportionality of corresponding sides of similar triangles, obtain BD/AB = BM/BC = DM/AC. The problem states AB = 2BD, so BD/AB = 1/2, hence BM/BC = 1/2 and DM/AC = 1/2. Because C, B, and M are collinear, ∠BCD = ∠MCD. In right triangle CDM, tan∠MCD = DM/CM = 2/3. Let DM = 2k, then CM = 3k. Also BM/BC = 1/2, so BM = BC/2; and C, B, and M are collinear and B is between C and M, so CM = BC + BM = BC + BC/2 = 3BC/2. From CM = 3k, get 3BC/2 = 3k, so BC = 2k. From DM/AC = 1/2 and DM = 2k, get AC = 4k. Therefore AC/BC = 4k/2k = 2.
